related_questions.question: Do I need to fill out a form to enter Italy?

text_blocks.snippet: For US citizens traveling to Italy for tourism, business, or short-term study (less than 90 days), you will need to fill out an online Passenger Locator Form (dPLF) before arrival, and you may also need to show proof of vaccination, a recovery certificate, or a negative COVID-19 test. If staying longer than 90 days, you'll need a visa and a permit to stay.
snippet_highlighted_words: you will need to fill out an online Passenger Locator Form (dPLF) before arrival

list.title: ETIAS:
list.snippet: If you are from a country that requires ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorization System), like the US, you will need to apply for authorization before travel. This applies to short-term visits for tourism, business, family visits, or short-term study (under 90 days).

list.title: Passenger Locator Form (dPLF):
list.snippet: This form is mandatory for all travelers entering Italy, regardless of vaccination status or origin. It can be filled out digitally online.

list.title: COVID-19 related documents:
list.snippet: Depending on the current regulations, you may be required to present a COVID-19 vaccination certificate, a certificate of recovery from COVID-19, or a negative COVID-19 test (molecular or antigen).

list.title: Visa requirements:
list.snippet: US citizens can enter Italy for up to 90 days without a visa for tourism or business. For stays longer than 90 days, a visa is required.

list.title: Permit to stay:
list.snippet: If you intend to live or stay in Italy for longer than 90 days, you will need to apply for a visa and obtain a permit to stay (permesso di soggiorno).

related_questions.question: Is the COVID pandemic still going on?

text_blocks.snippet: While the World Health Organization (WHO) declared an end to the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on May 5, 2023, COVID-19 continues to circulate. The pandemic's official end is not clearly defined, and whether it's still considered a pandemic depends on the definition used. Currently, COVID-19 vaccines continue to offer protection against severe disease and death according to the WHO.
